P·21  ·  SOVEREIGN INFRASTRUCTURE  ·  ON THE VF BUILD SLATE

NAV·ITA navigator that never sells your route.

Mainstream mapping apps know where you go. NAV·IT is the alternative: a self-hosted turn-by-turn navigator built on open map data, our own routing, our own tiles, our own edge. Zero third-party trackers. Every route stays yours; the architecture enforces it. Ships inside FuelIT and MapIT.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Every FuelIT drive ended
in somebody else's data.

You tap Go on a fuel stop. FuelIT hands you to Google Maps. From that moment, Google knows the route you're driving, the station you chose, and, by inference, that you used FuelIT to pick it. The "no data sold" promise had a hole the shape of a map tile.

F·01

The handoff is the leak

Consumer navigators are ad + data businesses. The moment your phone opens Google Maps or Waze with a destination in the URL, the platform logs that destination, joins it to your device identifier, retains it, and uses it to train models sold to third parties. The privacy claim of the pre-handoff app doesn't survive the tap.

F·02

Their SDK is not neutral

Even the "we run our own map" alternatives usually mean: our own logo, someone else's SDK. Google Maps SDK, Mapbox SDK and Apple MapKit all phone home from every device that installs them, keyed to a device fingerprint. The app doesn't tell you that the map you see phones home.

F·03

Offline is a hoax

Mainstream navigators all advertise "download maps for offline", and all of them stitch the offline session's routes into your online profile the moment you open the app online for anything else: traffic, search, ETA. No product on the shelf makes offline mean offline.

F·04

Live traffic costs your location

Real-time traffic requires broadcasting the live position of vehicles, yours or others', to whoever is building the model. HERE and TomTom sell that. Google collects it via every Android in a car. No product on the market offers live traffic without location telemetry. You pay with money or with position.

EVERY MAP TILE CAN BE PRIVATELY SERVED. THE INDUSTRY CHOSE NOT TO
WHO IT SERVES

Built for anyone whose route
shouldn't be someone's data.

Our own products first

FuelIT and MapIT can't credibly promise "no data sold" while handing every drive to Google. Fixing that took building an entire navigator, and we're not the only ones who want it. NAV·IT proves itself on our own products first: FuelIT ships with it, MapIT ships on it. We test every claim on the VF network's daily drives before it reaches the public.

FUELIT · SHIPS INSIDEMAPIT · RUNS ONVF NETWORK · PROVEN

Long-haul & cross-border drivers

People who cross Europe every week and dislike sharing their entire route history with a US ad platform. Offline packs work in every tunnel, mountain pass and mobile-signal gap.

Fleets that owe their drivers privacy

Van and small-fleet operators. Insurers, fuel-card brokers and every installed consumer navigator track their drivers; NAV·IT hands the operator route quality without handing anyone else a driving profile.

Journalists, lawyers, activists

Anyone whose destination is confidential by profession. Full-offline mode produces zero network traffic during navigation: verified by packet trace, documented in the threat model, backed by a bug bounty for anyone who can break the claim.

De-Googled Android + Linux phone users

NAV·IT has no dependency on Google Play Services. Runs on GrapheneOS, /e/OS, LineageOS. Runs on PinePhone. Runs on the phones the mainstream mapping apps refuse to ship for, because those users were already asking for this product.

WHAT IT CHANGES

From "trust us"
to "check the trace."

The measure of a privacy-first navigator is what a packet capture of a full drive contains. We judge NAV·IT on evidence, published in git, reproducible by anyone.

Three modes, one guarantee.

Full-offline: zero network traffic during navigation. Hybrid (default): routing over our anonymising Cloudflare gateway that strips your IP before origin. Online: same guarantee, no local cache required. Never a third-party origin.

Open primitives, signed responses.

OpenStreetMap data, Valhalla routing, Photon geocoding, MapLibre rendering, all Apache-2 / BSD / MIT. Our origin box Ed25519-signs every routing response; a compromised CDN cannot forge routes.

Verifiable by an outsider.

Public engineering spec. Public threat model. Public privacy model. Reproducible verification checklist for auditors. Bug bounty (€500–€25 000) for anyone who can break a claim. Trust is what you can prove.

THE MECHANICS

Four layers,
every one auditable.

Built the VF way: open primitives, our own infrastructure, cryptographic guarantees, public specs. Every layer answers a specific privacy question, with code you can read. Like every VF system, it leaves the lab with the engine fitted and the harness tuned.

LAYER 1

Open data plane

OpenStreetMap planet mirror on our own build box. Weekly diffs. No proprietary data licence to renew, no vendor to lock us in. Signed provenance: every published pack ships with the SHA-256 of the exact planet PBF it was built from and the git SHA of the tools that built it.

LAYER 2

Sovereign origin

Fastify server on a Hetzner AX102 in Germany. Valhalla for routing, Photon for search, PMTiles for tiles. Ed25519 origin signing key held only on the box. HMAC-authenticated requests. Boot-time refusal if any log configuration would serialise coordinates. The origin cannot lie undetected.

LAYER 3

Anonymising edge

Cloudflare Worker gateway strips CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For, User-Agent before origin sees them. Rate-limiting by rolling per-minute HMAC token; we don't need to see IP. 24h edge log retention, IP field-masked at ingest.

LAYER 4

Cryptographic clients

iOS uses CryptoKit's Curve25519 to verify every routing response against the origin's compiled-in public key. Android uses JDK 15+ native Ed25519. A tampered response is refused. Offline packs are Ed25519-signed too, verified at download and at every load. A hostile CDN cannot forge routes.

NEXT
R·03

MapIT: a standalone product on the same engine

We built NAV·IT for FuelIT, but the engine is general. MapIT ships as a full consumer navigator on the same infrastructure: same privacy guarantees, same offline packs, same signed responses. One backend, two products.

PLANNED
R·04

Probe-data traffic layer: opt-in, k-anonymised

Live traffic without location broadcast. Users who opt in send OSM segment IDs + speed + hour-of-week: no coordinates, no session, no fine-grained timestamps. We publish it back only when k≥50 contributors are pooled per segment-hour. Off by default, forever.

QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Does NAV·IT work offline?

Yes. Full-offline mode produces zero network traffic during navigation, verified by packet trace and documented in the threat model. You download Ed25519-signed region packs, from 50 MB for Malta to 1.5 GB for Germany, verified at download and at every load. Hybrid mode, the default, needs no local storage and routes through VF's anonymising gateway instead.

Does NAV·IT send my route to Google, Apple or Mapbox?

No. NAV·IT runs on OpenStreetMap data with Valhalla routing, Photon geocoding and MapLibre rendering, served from VF's own origin box in Germany. There is no third-party mapping SDK on the device. In hybrid mode the only network contact is navigator.vfempire.com, through a Cloudflare Worker gateway that strips your IP before the origin sees the request.

Can I buy NAV·IT on its own?

NAV·IT is infrastructure. It ships inside FuelIT and MapIT; you pay for those, and NAV·IT is included at every FuelIT tier. VF never monetises it as a standalone data business, an ad platform or an SDK sold to third parties. If that ever changes, a superseding ADR appears in git the same day.

Which phones does NAV·IT support?

iPhone on iOS 16+, Android 10+ with no Google Play Services requirement, or any modern web browser. It runs on GrapheneOS, /e/OS and LineageOS, and on the PinePhone. iOS verifies every routing response with CryptoKit's Curve25519; Android uses native JDK 15+ Ed25519. A tampered response is refused, so a hostile CDN cannot forge routes.

Which countries does NAV·IT cover at launch?

R·01 ships inside FuelIT for the FuelIT-9: Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Austria, the UK, Portugal, Malta and Luxembourg, with full-offline and hybrid modes and downloadable signed region packs. R·02 brings NAV·IT's own map to CarPlay and Android Auto. R·03 makes MapIT a standalone navigator on the same engine, and R·04 adds an opt-in, k-anonymised traffic layer.

How can I verify the privacy claims myself?

The engineering spec, threat model and privacy model are published, plus a verification checklist with seven reproducible checks for external auditors: packet-trace commands, signature-verification steps and a log-inspection procedure. VF's origin box Ed25519-signs every routing response. A bug bounty from €500 to €25 000 pays anyone who runs the checklist and breaks a claim.
